chain/chain: Often one function feeds another. Here x goes in and u comes out, where u is three x plus one.
chain/feed: Then u feeds a second function: z is u squared.
chain/nest: In one line, z is three x plus one, squared. Three x plus one is the inside. The squaring wrapped around it is the outside.
chain/vals: At x equals one, u is four, and z is sixteen. How fast does z change when x is nudged? That rate is written d z, d x, read “d z, d x”: the derivative of z with respect to x, a tiny change in z over the tiny change in x that caused it.
local/du: Each link has its own local slope. The inside, u equals three x plus one, moves three times as fast as x: d u, d x is three.
local/dz: The outside, z equals u squared, has slope two u. At u equals four, d z, d u is eight, also written z prime of four is eight.
local/nudge: Now nudge x by zero point zero one. u moves three times that, zero point zero three. And z moves eight times that, zero point two four.
local/mult: So z moves three times eight, twenty four times as fast as x. That is the chain rule: multiply the local slopes, d z, d x equals d z, d u times d u, d x.
back/longer: A chain can be as long as you like. Here x feeds u, u feeds v, and v feeds z. At the current point, the local slopes are three, minus two, and a half. What is d z, d x?
back/back: Start at the end and walk backwards, multiplying as you go: a half, times minus two is minus one, times three is minus three.
back/backprop: So d z, d x is minus three. On the way, the walk also found the slope of z with respect to v and to u.
